routing_warnings.description: The request for a complementary website and materials font belongs to brand font guidance rather than the custom logo letterform design.
The client's request for complementary font recommendations belongs to the separate brand font guidance Requirement.
The supplied companion-font recommendations implement the brand font guidance Requirement rather than modifying the custom logo letterforms.
The request for only three separate colour versions concerns the export-variant deliverable rather than colours within the main logo artwork.
The inaccessible colour-codes document concerns delivery of the brand colour specification, not the approved artwork's colour treatment.
The repeated inability to open the colour-codes document belongs to the brand colour specification Requirement.
Supplying the logo colour codes is an implementation claim for the brand colour specification Requirement.
The statement that the black-box background will not suit every use directly establishes the need for background variants rather than verifying general cross-media logo suitability.
The suitability statement concerns editable source-file formats for print, web, social media, signage, and merchandise rather than the inherent cross-media suitability of the logo design.
The requested U, H, and D revisions concern specific letterform proportions and decorative features rather than selection of the overall composition.
The reported failure of most PNG files concerns the usability of PNG exports, not which colour variants are required.
The inaccessible colour-codes document concerns the separate brand-colour specification deliverable.
The client's preference for the draft logo's colours concerns the artwork's visual colour treatment, not the colour-reference deliverable.
The graduated colours requested for the selected logo concern its visual colour treatment rather than documentation of brand colour codes.
The claim that the logo lettering is completely custom-made concerns the letterform design specifically and does not establish originality or trademark suitability for the entire logo.
The client requests written confirmation of copyright ownership for future trademark activity, which belongs to the separate ownership-confirmation Requirement.
The lines beside the strapline and proposed outline or brightness changes concern strapline presentation rather than its content.
Matching the strapline to GLOBAL with graduated colours changes the logo colour treatment rather than the strapline content.
The selected graduated-orange treatment for the strapline concerns the approved main-logo colour configuration rather than strapline content.

The request to disclose whether the logo uses an existing font or custom lettering belongs to the separate lettering-origin Requirement; only the complementary-font request concerns the target Requirement.

The statement that the logo lettering is completely custom-made directly supports the separate lettering-origin Requirement; the offer to suggest complementary fonts is not yet a completed deliverable.
